data.title: RTX’s Pratt & Whitney advances F-35 engine upgrade toward production
data.description:
RTX’s (RTX) Pratt & Whitney has completed a design review of its planned F135 Engine Core Upgrade, advancing the program toward production for the F-35 fighter jet.

The risk reduction design review examined the upgrade’s detailed design, propulsion technologies, aircraft integration and testing preparations. It also assessed whether suppliers are prepared to support production and retrofits.

The upgrade is intended to provide the additional power and thermal-management capacity required for the F-35’s Block 4 modernization program. Block 4 calls for advanced sensors, weapons and other systems across all three variants of the aircraft.

For investors, the milestone reduces some of the technical and execution risk surrounding a program that could support long-term production and aftermarket revenue for RTX (RTX). The ability to retrofit existing aircraft also expands the potential market beyond newly built F-35s, although future revenue will depend on government funding, testing results and the timing of production contracts.

Pratt & Whitney Military Engines President Jill Albertelli said in a statement that the review demonstrated the design’s maturity and moved the company closer to delivering an upgrade based on the existing F135 architecture. U.S. Navy Capt. Mitch Grant, the F-35 propulsion program manager, said the project remains on schedule to support the aircraft’s modernization.

Risk-reduction work funded under a contract awarded in 2024 includes design development, aircraft integration, test preparation, engineering and supply-chain readiness. Pratt & Whitney said the upgrade is designed to be installed in newly produced aircraft or retrofitted at F135 maintenance depots.

The company has delivered more than 1,500 F135 engines to customers across 20 allied countries. Pratt & Whitney plans to retain substantial commonality with the current engine as it develops the upgrade, potentially limiting changes to the F-35’s existing production and maintenance network.

data.title: Wells Fargo cuts S&P 500 target to 7,700, sees 5-10% downside first
data.description:
Wells Fargo cut its year-end S&P 500 (SP500) (SPY) (VOO) (IVV) target to 7,700 from 7,950, saying the index has limited upside from current levels and could fall 5%-10% first as the market enters the late innings of the earnings cycle.

Analyst Ohsung Kwon said the team has turned more cautious heading into September even as it raised its earnings forecasts to $425 for 2027 and $460 for 2028. Wells Fargo expects multiple compression to offset some of that earnings strength.

One of the biggest concerns is investor allocation. Kwon estimates equities now account for 72% of portfolios versus fixed income, the highest level since 1969. With the 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) nearing 5%, the firm calculates a fair equity allocation of roughly 60%, leaving a 12-percentage-point gap between actual and fair exposure.

That gap is the widest since 1969 and exceeds the level seen during the tech bubble. Historically, the spread has had a strong relationship with forward five-year equity excess returns, suggesting relatively limited upside from stocks versus bonds from here.

The firm also changed its sector stance, downgrading Technology (XLK) to Equal Weight from Overweight while upgrading Health Care (XLV) to Overweight from Equal Weight.

Within Technology, Kwon continues to prefer Software (IGV) over Semiconductors (SOXX) (SMH). He sees political pushback against datacenter development as a growing risk and also flagged the stronger Korean won as a potential headwind for Samsung and SK Hynix, which could weigh on the broader memory trade. Kwon expects semiconductors to at least retest their July lows.

Health Care, by contrast, could benefit from a more defensive market backdrop. Wells Fargo also sees a potential Democratic sweep in the midterms as a positive for the sector, particularly if enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies are restored.

data.title: Connect Biopharma drops as asthma candidate fails in mid-stage trial
data.description:
Connect Biopharma (CNTB) lost nearly 40% in premarket trading on Tuesday after announcing that its lead candidate, rademikibart, failed to reach the primary endpoint in a Phase 2 trial for patients with asthma.

The global trial, designed to evaluate rademikibart as an add-on therapy for acute exacerbations in adults and adolescents with asthma and type 2 inflammation, had treatment failure as its primary endpoint.

While the injectable cut the treatment failure rate by roughly 66% over 28 days compared to placebo, the effect was not statistically significant, Connect Biopharma (CNTB) said, citing topline data from the 160-subject study named Seabreeze STAT Asthma.

However, the company noted a statistically significant improvement in a key secondary endpoint called the absolute one-week change in post-bronchodilator (post-BD) forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), which it has selected as a proposed primary endpoint in Phase 3.

The experimental therapy was well tolerated with no new safety signals, the San Diego, California-based biopharma added.

Topline data from its Phase 2 Seabreeze STAT COPD study in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is expected later this month, after which the company plans to meet with the FDA to discuss late-stage trial plans for rademikibart.

data.title: MediaTek takes aim at Qualcomm with TSMC-built 2-nanometer chip
data.description:
MediaTek unveiled a new flagship smartphone processor built with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's (TSMC) most advanced chipmaking technology, stepping up its push into the premium handset market and the growing on-device artificial intelligence business.

The Dimensity 9600 Pro is MediaTek’s first smartphone processor manufactured using TSMC’s 2-nanometer process, the company said Tuesday. It also introduced the Dimensity 9600M, produced on TSMC’s 3-nanometer technology and targeting a wider portion of the flagship segment. Phones using both processors are expected to reach the market soon.

The 9600 Pro features a dedicated neural-processing unit designed to run more sophisticated generative AI workloads directly on smartphones. MediaTek said the component improves prompt processing by 51% from the prior generation before an AI model begins producing an answer.

The launch comes as MediaTek seeks to gain ground on Qualcomm (QCOM) in higher-end smartphones, where rising prices and demand for AI capabilities are creating opportunities for chipmakers to capture better margins. MediaTek’s market value surpassed Qualcomm’s (QCOM) earlier this year.

The company is also expanding beyond handsets into AI infrastructure and custom silicon. Its first AI accelerator developed for a major US cloud provider is expected to enter mass production in the fourth quarter.

MediaTek raised $3.9 billion through a convertible bond sale last month, with Nvidia (NVDA) investing $3.5 billion and Alphabet (GOOG) also participating.

data.title: NFI’s New Flyer wins order for 12 CNG buses
data.description:
• NFI Group (NFI) said its New Flyer subsidiary was awarded a contract by the Central Ohio Transit Authority for up to 45 60-foot Xcelsior CNG heavy-duty transit buses.
  • The contract includes a firm order for 12 buses and options for up to 33 additional buses.
  • The firm order will be added to NFI’s Q3 2026 backlog, while the option buses will be added to its option backlog.
  • The buses will replace aging vehicles and support new bus rapid transit service in Columbus. The purchase is backed by the federal Low-No Grant Program.
  • New Flyer has delivered more than 230 buses to COTA since 2000, including 102 CNG buses.

data.title: Airbus sees Asia-Pacific jet demand holding firm despite global headwinds
data.description:
Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) continues to see robust demand for commercial aircraft, with airlines showing little sign that geopolitical tensions or supply-chain disruptions are weakening their appetite for new jets.

Anand Stanley, president of Airbus Asia-Pacific, said during a market outlook briefing in Hong Kong that customers remain eager to accept aircraft, Reuters reported Tuesday. Delivery activity also is strengthening in Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and other regions.

The European aircraft manufacturer has delivered 9% more planes so far this year than during the comparable period of 2025, according to Stanley.

For Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) investors, steady demand and rising deliveries support the outlook for revenue, cash flow and production growth. The company already has a substantial order backlog, so its near-term financial performance depends less on finding buyers than on securing engines, components and labor to build aircraft on schedule. Asia-Pacific’s projected share of worldwide deliveries also gives Airbus significant exposure to one of aviation’s strongest long-term growth markets. The main investor risk remains execution: demand can be abundant while supply constraints delay deliveries and the payments tied to them.

Asia-Pacific to claim nearly half of new aircraft

Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) estimates that airlines worldwide will require approximately 42,000 new aircraft during the next two decades. About 45% of those planes are expected to go to Asia-Pacific customers as passenger traffic expands and carriers replace older fleets.

China alone is projected to need 8,830 new passenger aircraft during the period, making it Airbus’ largest individual commercial aviation market. India is expected to require 3,480 aircraft, while the remainder of Asia-Pacific will account for another 6,880.

François Cabaret, who leads Airbus’ global market forecasting, said Chinese airlines have fallen behind their previous fleet-renewal pace. Before the pandemic, carriers in China accepted about 400 aircraft annually. Combined deliveries from Airbus, Boeing and COMAC have since dropped to fewer than half that level.

That gap creates potential for a sizable replacement cycle, although the timing will depend on China’s economic growth, airline finances and the ability of manufacturers to increase production.

India accelerates as China forecast cools

Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) expects passenger traffic across Asia to grow by an average of 5.1% a year over the next two decades, but that expansion will not be evenly distributed.

India remains the fastest-growing major aviation market. Airbus increased its forecast for annual domestic traffic growth in the country to 9.3% from 8.9%.

The company lowered its comparable projection for China to 4.7% from 5.4%. Cabaret attributed the reduction to the country’s broader economic conditions rather than an excessive supply of aircraft or airline capacity.

Smaller cities create new routes

Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) also expects urban growth to create demand beyond Asia’s largest metropolitan areas. Approximately 600 new small and midsize cities could emerge around the world over the next 20 years, supporting additional airports and routes.

The company sees its A220 and A321XLR as well suited to that shift. Airlines have used the smaller A220 to establish more than 400 routes worldwide, and Airbus believes the aircraft could make another 800 city pairs viable in Asia-Pacific.

The longer-range A321XLR could create more than 2,200 additional route opportunities in the region. Its ability to fly distances traditionally served by wide-body aircraft gives airlines a way to test thinner international routes without committing to a much larger plane.

data.title: ScottsMiracle-Gro redeems $250M in notes, begins share buyback
data.description:
ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) said Tuesday it redeemed $250 million of senior notes, renewed a major financing facility and began buying back shares as the lawn and garden products company works to reduce debt while returning capital to stockholders.

The company redeemed all of its 5.25% senior notes due in 2026 on Sept. 11. It funded the repayment with borrowings under its revolving credit facility and excess free cash flow expected during fiscal 2026.

ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) also renewed a $750 million accounts receivable facility with J.P. Morgan Chase, extending its maturity through Aug. 31, 2027. Such facilities let companies obtain liquidity using customer receivables and can help support working-capital needs.

For investors, the debt repayment removes a near-term maturity but does not eliminate the obligation because ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) partly replaced the notes with revolver borrowings. The company’s projected $275 million in free cash flow could help reduce that balance. Meanwhile, the buyback may support per-share results, though management said debt reduction will take priority over additional repurchases.

ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) spent $25 million repurchasing shares in August, beginning a previously authorized $500 million program. The company said the pace and size of future purchases will depend on market conditions, leverage goals and other financial priorities.

The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 forecast, including low-single-digit sales growth in its U.S. Consumer business, adjusted gross margin of at least 32% and adjusted earnings of $4.30 to $4.45 a share. It continues to expect mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth, $275 million in free cash flow and a year-end leverage ratio in the high-three-times range.

ScottsMiracle-Gro’s (SMG) fiscal year ends Sept. 30. The company plans to report its full-year results on Nov. 4.
